newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union to restart Lufthansa talks.
newsitem.headline: German union to restart Lufthansa talks.

text.p: German white-collar trade union DAG, the Deutsche Angestellten-Gewerkschaft, said on Monday it had agreed to hold new talks with Deutsche Lufthansa AG about ways of resolving their wage dispute.
The airline was earlier forced to cancel 35 flights while a further 46 were delayed as a result of a two-hour strike by German flight crews and ground staff organised by DAG.

"DAG has meanwhile accepted an offer by Lufthansa to discuss on November 19 how to proceed further in the wage dispute," DAG chief negotiator Michael Tarp said in a statement. The union said no further action had been scheduled.
Talks between the two ended last month after Lufthansa failed to meet DAG's demand for a four percent increase in wages.
DAG said Monday's industrial action was also a protest against Lufthansa's push for the new wage contract to extend over a 27-month period.

DAG fears that such a contract length would allow the airline to introduce new measures such as out-sourcing of ancillary services and to set up subsidiaries not covered by existing agreements on working conditions.
